# MemOS

> Local-first, persistent memory layer for AI agents. SQLite on your own
> machine, no cloud and no API keys. TypeScript SDK, Python server, MCP
> tools, document ingestion, and reproducible retrieval benchmarks.
>
> Packages: npm `@mem-os/sdk`, PyPI `mem-os-python`.

Use this file to choose the right page. Every link is the canonical docs
page; the repository has runnable examples under `examples/` and benchmark
methodology under `benchmarks/README.md`.

## Documentation

- [Overview](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index/): MemOS is a local-first memory layer for AI agents. It stores facts, preferences, decisions, and ingested documents in a single SQLite file, then recalls them through a TypeScrip...
- [Installation](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/installation/): Let's get MemOS running on your machine. Pick your path below — every one of them ends with the same thing: a memory layer that works entirely offline.
- [Your first memory](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/quickstart-ingest/): This is the shortest path from a folder of notes to a memory you can search. No account, no API key, no cloud.
- [Harness matrix](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/harness-matrix/): MemOS is a plain stdio MCP server. That makes it portable, but each harness has its own config key, file location, and plugin format. This page maps the ones worth supporting, w...
- [Website and harness audit](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/research/2026-11-website-harness-audit/): Research notes behind the redesign and the harness support added this month.
- [Memory model](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/concepts/): MemOS is not a chat log with a search box. It is a small graph of durable memories with provenance, time bounds, and an explicit deletion path. This page explains the objects yo...
- [Fidelity levels](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/fidelity-levels/): Every memory exists at four fidelity levels. The retriever picks the **cheapest level that satisfies the query** instead of always returning verbatim text — the single biggest t...
- [Temporal events and reminders](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/temporal-events/): MemOS extracts **scheduled events** from plain utterances, lets any harness reschedule or cancel them in natural language, and surfaces **due reminders** — all **deterministical...
- [Recall inspector, feedback, and health](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/recall-inspector/): Three related surfaces for answering questions that ordinary retrieval cannot:
- [Memory operations](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/memory-guide/): Everything you can do with a running MemOS store beyond the basic store/search loop. Every command below works through the TypeScript SDK, the CLI, and the MCP server unless noted.
- [Document ingestion](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ingestion/): Point MemOS at a folder and it remembers what is in it. Markdown, text, CSV, JSON, YAML, HTML and PDF are supported. No cloud, no upload, no API key.
- [Preferences](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/preferences/): Facts are easy to retrieve: the question names the thing, so keyword and embedding search both find it. Preferences are not. "What would I enjoy this weekend?" shares no words w...
- [Cross-harness sync](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/cross-harness/): MemOS ships as a plugin for many agent harnesses (Claude Code, Cline, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenClaw, …), but the memory itself was never tied to any of them. This feature makes th...
- [Adapters](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/adapters/): Adapters bridge MemOS with AI frameworks. They handle memory retrieval (injecting context before a model call) and memory storage (extracting facts from conversations).
- [Integrations](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/integrations/): MemOS ships as a **plain stdio MCP server** — the one integration surface that Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, OpenCode, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and every other MCP-capable...
- [UMT and MemOS config](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/umt-integration/): The Universal MCP Toolkit and MemOS agree on one configuration surface: the environment. Nothing is copied into a second settings file, and no secret is written in plaintext by...
- [LLM Guardian integration](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guardian-integration/): LLM Guardian sits between an app and the model. MemOS can supply a token-budgeted context pack that Guardian injects as a system shard. Guardian can optionally fold that pack be...
- [Remote MCP and OAuth](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/remote-mcp/): MemOS ships **local-only by default**. There is no hosted MemOS endpoint and no account. The optional Streamable HTTP transport exists so you can self-host it for a team or a re...
- [CLI commands](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/cli/): Generated from `src/cli-help.ts` by `npm run docs:reference`. Every command in the dispatch table is listed; if it is not here, it is not a command.
- [MCP tools](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/mcp-tools/): Generated from `src/mcp.ts` by `npm run docs:reference`. The default profile exposes the core set; `MEMOS_MCP_TOOLS=all` exposes every tool listed here.
- [HTTP API](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/http-api/): Generated from the FastAPI OpenAPI document (MemOS 1.6.27). The server mounts every route under `/api/mem`.
- [TypeScript API](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api-reference/): Complete reference for the MemOS TypeScript SDK and Python HTTP API.
- [MCP compatibility](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/mcp-compatibility/): MemOS speaks the Model Context Protocol over **stdio** and **Streamable HTTP**. This document states which revisions we support, how we test them, and when we remove old ones.
- [Memory Explorer (MCP App)](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/mcp-apps-explorer/): An interactive memory-graph explorer served as a `ui://` resource (`ui://memos/explorer`) under MCP Apps (ratified January 2026). It renders the MemOS entity/memory graph as a s...
- [Documentation coverage](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/coverage/): Generated by `npm run docs:coverage`. A mention means the exact identifier appears somewhere in `README.md`, `llms-install.md`, `docs/`, or `plugin/skills/`. It is a floor, not...
- [Security model](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/security-model/): MemOS is local-first, which removes a class of risk but not all of it. This page states what is protected by default and what the operator must do.
- [Operations runbook](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/operations/): How to run a MemOS store over months rather than a demo.
- [Troubleshooting](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/troubleshooting/): Symptom → diagnose → fix for the failure modes MemOS users actually hit. Run **`memos doctor`** first — it's the one-command health check for the store, embedding config, and en...
- [How we benchmark](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/benchmarking/): MemOS should only publish benchmark claims that can be reproduced from a clean checkout. The most useful comparison is not raw model quality; it is whether a memory layer can st...
- [Results in plain English](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/benchmark-results/): No judge model. No "vibes" scoring. These numbers ask one question: **when you ask MemOS about something from the past, does it actually return the right memory?**
- [Comparison table](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/benchmark-comparison/): This document is a **head-to-head snapshot**, not a marketing piece. We cite published numbers from each vendor's own evaluation papers and tag every row with the methodology th...
- [Benchmark quality](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/benchmark-quality/): This is a **synthetic regression harness**, not a leaderboard number. It measures that retrieval quality does not regress between builds, on a small fixed dataset that ships in...
- [Accuracy roadmap](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/accuracy-roadmap/): This page separates **shipped accuracy work** from **runs that still need an external model, dataset, or submission**. The goal is to make every number in the README reproducibl...
- [AI Trio contracts](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ai-trio-contracts/): MemOS is the local memory layer in the AI Trio. It should retrieve and score context, preserve provenance, and expose compact read-only context packs before any agent mutates me...
- [Beta channel](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/beta-updates/): Run the latest verified code — not just the latest npm publish. The beta channel tracks every **fully-successful main commit**: a commit counts only when the latest runs of the...
- [Local Dashboard](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/dashboard/): A browser-based UI for your MemOS memory store. No MCP Apps host required — just run `memos dashboard` and a local web server starts serving an interactive dashboard.
- [MemOS feature roadmap — demand, gaps, and plugin integration](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/feature-roadmap-2026/): Demand signals came from: competing memory-layer READMEs and docs (supermemory, mem0, Zep, Letta), third-party comparison write-ups (Mnemoverse Q3 2026, Vectorize, EverMind, Med...

- [Provenance Trust](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/provenance-trust/): **The write-gate that keeps poisoned content out of your agent's recall — no cloud, no LLM on the hot path.**
- [Session Hooks](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/session-hooks/): Automatically extract durable facts when a coding session ends. MemOS provides session-end hooks for Claude Code and OpenCode that run `memos session-hook`, parse the session tr...
- [Encrypted Sync](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/sync/): Sync memories between machines using encrypted bundle files. The bundle is encrypted with AES-256-GCM before it touches disk — your cloud drive, USB stick, or email never sees p...
- [Tamper-evident mutation log](https://memos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tamper-log/): Every memory mutation — `store`, `import`, `update`, `forget` — appends one entry to an append-only, hash-chained log stored in the `tamper_log` table of the same database. Each...
